A change of metric scope is not training divergence

Controlled MLflow 3.17.1 logging only: twenty improving unqualified losses followed by twenty model/dataset losses. Native SQLite exposes both in one run aggregate. The report preserves every recorded value but cannot diagnose it as one training curve.

Input incomplete

  • 1 MLflow metric key has linked model/dataset records. Their run-level aggregates retain all recorded values under explicit names, without mapping them to canonical diagnostic metrics. Export one model/dataset history to diagnose it; a run aggregate cannot recover its source scopes.
  • MLflow run 'mixed-dataset' (094ea54767b24a8895e0876c978ac4c6), experiment 1; recorded status FINISHED, lifecycle active.
  • MLflow SQL backends can normalize infinities to finite extremes. This reader restores native NaN flags but cannot reconstruct infinities already replaced by the backend.
  • The horizontal axis retains MLflow's caller-supplied step values; they do not establish optimizer-update counts. Native defaults can repeat step 0. Use --step-key step only when this counter measures training updates.

Timing unavailable

Wall-clock timing needs an explicit training-step column; this source uses MLflow logged steps. Logging intervals cannot establish seconds per training step. Log step counts, step_time, or throughput, or select a training counter with --step-key.

Timing sources and windows

Coordinates: step (logging steps).

Default timing check: first and last 20% of observations, at least five each, without overlap. This describes those windows, not every step of the run. Direct throughput is time per reported unit (such as a sample or token). Unavailable timing does not establish stable speed.
